Afro House: African percussion patterns, tribal drum rhythms, djembe and shaker grooves layered over a four-on-the-floor kick. Organic textures, vocal chants, warm mid-range basslines, earthy instruments mixed with electronic production.
Deep House: Warm filtered bassline, smooth chord pads, jazzy or soulful chord progressions. Laid-back groove with a soft kick, subtle shuffled hi-hats, and lush atmospheric pads. Mellow, warm, and understated.
House: Classic four-on-the-floor kick drum pattern, offbeat hi-hats, synth stabs, and piano chords. Balanced mid-tempo groove, clear vocal hooks, uplifting energy with consistent driving rhythm.
Tech House: Groovy, minimal, percussive with a tight rolling bassline. Repetitive loops, crisp hi-hats, clicky percussion, functional DJ tool sound. Less melodic, more groove-focused than House.
Disco House: Funky basslines, disco string samples, filtered loops from 70s-80s records. Choppy guitar riffs, handclaps, and orchestral hits over a modern house kick pattern.
Electro House: Heavy, distorted bassline with aggressive synth leads. Big room energy, massive drops, saw wave leads, hard-hitting kicks and snares. Festival-oriented, maximalist production.
Progressive House: Long, evolving build-ups with layered synth melodies. Atmospheric pads, arpeggiated sequences, delayed plucks, and a gradual energy arc. Melodic but structured for DJ mixing.
Melodic Techno: Hypnotic arpeggios, atmospheric pad layers, driving four-on-the-floor kick. Emotional minor-key melodies over a relentless beat, reverb-drenched synths, and deep sub-bass.
Techno: Hard-hitting industrial kick drum, metallic hi-hats, sparse dark atmosphere. Repetitive mechanical loops, distorted synths, cold and clinical production. Minimal melodic content.
Hard Techno: Aggressive distorted kick, pounding industrial rhythm at fast tempo. Acid squelch sounds, harsh synth stabs, relentless percussive energy. Dark, abrasive, and intense.
Trance: Uplifting supersaw pads, long euphoric breakdowns, pulsating bassline. Arpeggiated synth lines, emotional chord progressions, soaring leads, and anthem-like energy builds.
Psytrance: Rapid psychedelic arpeggios, squelchy acid bassline, extremely fast tempo. Trippy layered FX, alien sound design, hypnotic repetitive patterns, intense driving energy.
Breakbeat: Syncopated broken drum patterns instead of four-on-the-floor. Funky sampled breakbeats, chopped drum loops, energetic but unpredictable rhythms with electronic production.
Drum & Bass: Very fast breakbeat with heavy sub-bass. Rapid syncopated drums, choppy sampled breaks, deep rolling basslines, and high energy. Often with reese bass or amen break patterns.
UK Garage: Shuffled two-step drum pattern, skippy syncopated hi-hats, pitched-up vocal chops. Warm sub-bass, swinging groove, garage organ stabs, and a bouncy rhythmic feel.
Dubstep: Heavy wobble bass, half-time drum pattern, sub-bass drops. Dark atmosphere, sparse arrangements with massive low-frequency sound design and aggressive modulated basslines.
Trap: 808 bass with heavy sub, rapid hi-hat rolls, snappy snares. Sparse beat with dramatic drops, pitched vocal samples, and a slow but hard-hitting half-time feel. Hip-hop influenced electronic.
Eurodance: Catchy synth melodies, techno-pop beats, energetic female vocals with male rap verses. Bright, cheerful production with hands-up style synths and a fast club-friendly tempo.
IDM: Glitchy, complex, experimental electronic rhythms. Unusual time signatures, granular synthesis textures, detuned melodies, and cerebral abstract sound design. Intentionally non-danceable.
Synthwave: Retro 80s synthesizer sounds, analog pad textures, gated reverb drums. Nostalgic, cinematic atmosphere with arpeggiated sequences, neon-tinged melodies, and warm analog bass.
Synthpop: Catchy pop melodies with synthesizer-driven production. Electronic drums, sequenced bass, clean vocal delivery, and hook-driven arrangements. Polished, melodic, and accessible.
Ambient: Slow-evolving drone textures, vast atmospheric pads, minimal rhythm or none. Spacious reverbs, gentle tonal movements, and meditative soundscapes. Calm, immersive, ethereal.
Indie Dance: Guitars mixed with electronic beats, synth-rock crossover feel. Drum machines with live-sounding elements, indie vocals, dance-friendly but with band-like instrumentation.
Electro Swing: Swing-era jazz samples mixed with electronic beats. Brass sections, vintage vocal samples, double-time hi-hats, and a bouncy jazz rhythm over modern bass and drums.
Trip Hop: Downtempo breakbeat, dark moody atmosphere, vinyl crackle textures. Slow hip-hop drums with atmospheric pads, jazz samples, turntable scratches, and melancholic vocal delivery.
Pop: Catchy vocal melodies, polished radio-friendly production, clear verse-chorus structure. Bright synths or guitars, programmed drums, hook-driven, and commercially accessible sound.
Indie Pop: Jangly guitars, lo-fi or DIY production aesthetic, sweet vocal melodies. Light drums, warm analog tones, and a heartfelt intimate feel with less commercial polish than mainstream pop.
Post-Punk: Angular guitar riffs, driving bass lines, cold atmosphere. Reverb-drenched vocals, mechanical drum machine or stark drumming, dark and moody with a new wave energy.
New Wave: Synth-driven 80s pop-rock with bright keyboards, melodic hooks, and clean production. Drum machines mixed with live drums, quirky vocal delivery, and a polished retro-futuristic aesthetic.
Rock: Distorted electric guitars, powerful drum kit, bass guitar groove. Strong backbeat, guitar riffs and solos, raw energy, and a verse-chorus song structure with live band performance.
Indie Rock: Crunchy lo-fi guitars, raw unpolished production, energetic drumming. DIY aesthetic, distortion pedals, sincere vocal delivery, and an alternative underground sound.
Rock 'n' Roll: Classic 12-bar blues-based guitar riffs, driving shuffle beat, slap-back echo. Energetic upright or electric bass, boogie-woogie piano, and a raw vintage rockabilly feel.
Punk: Fast aggressive power chords, rapid drumming, shouted vocals. Minimal production, raw distorted guitars, short songs with high energy and a confrontational attitude.
Hip-Hop: Boom-bap or trap drum pattern, sampled loops or 808 bass. Rhythmic vocal delivery (rap), DJ scratches, bass-heavy mix, and a groove built around lyrical flow.
R&B: Smooth vocal melodies, lush chord progressions, mellow grooves. Warm bass, soft drum programming, tasteful synth pads, and a sophisticated soulful production aesthetic.
Reggaeton: Dembow rhythm pattern (tresillo-based), heavy kick and snare, Latin percussion. Repetitive reggaeton beat, urban bass, Spanish-language vocal flow, and a bouncy danceable groove.
Latin Pop: Latin rhythms with pop production — salsa or cumbia percussion, bright horns, and catchy vocal melodies. Warm guitars, Latin groove patterns, and accessible mainstream sound.
Reggae: Offbeat skank guitar strum, one-drop drum pattern, deep dub bass. Laid-back tempo, horn sections, organ bubble, and a relaxed island groove with heavy reverb on snare.
Dancehall: Digital reggae riddim, fast chatty vocal delivery, heavy bass drops. Electronic dancehall beat, gunshot sound effects, siren samples, and a energetic Caribbean street sound.
Ska: Upbeat offbeat guitar and horn stabs, walking bass line, fast tempo. Bright brass section (trumpet, trombone, saxophone), energetic drumming, and a choppy rhythmic feel.
Kuduro: Fast Angolan electronic dance rhythm, hard-hitting drum machine patterns. African vocal chants, percussive loops, minimal but intense production with a raw and energetic feel.
Afrobeats: Guitar highlife patterns, percussion-heavy groove, Afro-pop vocal melodies. Log drum programming, shaker rhythms, warm production, and a mid-tempo danceable West African feel.
Balkan: Brass band melodies, fast asymmetric time signatures (7/8, 9/8, 11/8). Clarinet and trumpet leads, driving percussion, accordion, and an energetic Eastern European folk dance sound.
Jazz: Improvised instrumental solos, swing or walking bass, brushed or swinging drums. Complex chord voicings, saxophone and trumpet melodies, dynamic live performance with musical conversation.
Disco: Four-on-the-floor kick, funky bass guitar, lush orchestral strings. Hi-hat patterns, handclaps, wah-wah guitar, and a glamorous 70s dancefloor energy with live instrumentation.
Funk: Syncopated bass guitar groove, tight rhythmic guitar scratches, horn stabs. Emphasis on the 'one' beat, James Brown-style drumming, clavinet, and a deep pocket feel.
Soul: Warm emotional vocals, gospel-influenced harmonies, live band instrumentation. Organ, horns, smooth bass, and a heartfelt expressive delivery with rich melodic content.
Blues: 12-bar blues progression, bent guitar notes, expressive vocal delivery. Slow to mid-tempo shuffle, harmonica, bass walking lines, and a raw emotive feeling with call-and-response structure.
